answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit and build verifiable work history before trading at full limits. Creating fake identities then becomes expensive: every clone must lock funds and wait through a slow reputation ramp, not simply copy a free account. A trusted record is like a sonnet, easy to recognize but hard to fake at scale, and a newcomer may not wander freely across markets until its past work checks out. Even a velvet-smooth pitch cannot bypass the stake or waiting period, so attackers pay per identity while honest agents pay once.
